_about: Parameters of sim/wind.py (LBM wind) and sim/trees.py (tree failure, debris, glazing, flood-driven cars). Every value has a source; 'calibrated' = tuned so the 31.12.2022 replay matches the 311 tree reports in the tile (see runs/dev_wind/); 'assumed' = engineering judgement, stated as such. Loaded by sim.trees.load_params().

wind_z0_inflow_m.source: Wieringa 1992, J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn. 41:357-368, updated Davenport roughness classification: class 6 'very rough' 0.5 m, class 7 'skimming' 1.0 m (dense city)

wind_z0_street_m.source: Wieringa 1992 (as above), class 4 'roughly open' 0.10 m: sub-grid street roughness (cars, furniture) beneath resolved buildings

von_karman.source: von Karman constant; Garratt 1992, The Atmospheric Boundary Layer, Cambridge UP

smagorinsky_cs.source: Lilly 1967, Proc. IBM Sci. Comput. Symp. Environ. Sci., 195-210 (Cs ~ 0.17 for isotropic turbulence)

lbm_u10_lattice.source: Kruger et al. 2017, The Lattice Boltzmann Method, Springer, sec. 7.3: compressibility error O(Ma^2); Ma = 0.05 at 10 m, 0.12 at lid

reynolds_independence.source: Snyder 1981, Guideline for Fluid Modeling of Atmospheric Diffusion, US EPA-600/8-81-009: flow around sharp-edged buildings is Re-independent above Re_H ~ 11,000 (storm Re_H ~ 1e8), so velocity scales linearly with the reference gust

velocity_pressure.source: ASCE 7-22 eq. 26.10-1 (SI): q = 0.613 K V^2; quasi-steady 3-s gust pressure, p = q Cp

glass_capacity_pre1980_kpa.source: ASTM E1300-16, load resistance of ~6 mm annealed monolithic lites ~1.5-2 m^2 under 3-s load: ~1.5-2.5 kPa

glass_capacity_post1980_kpa.source: ASTM E1300-16 glass type factor 2.0 for heat-strengthened glass (short duration) applied to insulating units; typical SF curtain-wall design pressures 1.9-3.4 kPa (ASCE 7 C&C)

tree_crown_length_frac.source: McPherson, van Doorn & Peper 2016, Urban Tree Database, USFS GTR PSW-253: crown height ~0.5-0.7 of tree height for street trees

tree_vogel_exponent.source: Vogel 1989, J. Exp. Bot. 40:941-948; Vollsinger et al. 2005, Can. J. For. Res. 35:1238-1249 (hardwood crowns, Cd*A ~ U^-b, b ~ 0.5-1.0); de Langre 2008, Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 40:141-168

tree_vogel_u0_ms.source: GALES streamlining onset: crown drag area constant below 10 m/s and reconfigures above (Gardiner et al. 2000, Ecol. Model. 129:1-23; Mayhead 1973, Agric. Meteorol. 12:123-130 wind-tunnel trees to 38 m/s)

tree_cd0.source: calibrated: chosen so the median critical breaking speed of sound (defect-free) trees in the inventory is ~42 m/s, Virot et al. 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93:023001; consistent with crown Cd 0.3-0.7 at low speed (Mayhead 1973, Agric. Meteorol. 12:123-130)

tree_gust_dyn_factor.source: quasi-static with 3-s gust; GALES gust factor already in the 3-s gust (Gardiner et al. 2000, Ecol. Model. 129:1-23)

wood_density_green.source: USDA FPL Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282 (2021) ch. 4: green hardwood density ~800-1100 kg/m3 above fibre saturation

stem_form_factor.source: stem volume = f * pi/4 * d^2 * H, form factor ~0.4-0.5 for broadleaves (Husch, Beers & Kershaw 2003, Forest Mensuration, 4th ed.)

uproot_creg_nm_per_kg.source: Nicoll, Gardiner, Rayner & Peace 2006, Can. J. For. Res. 36:1871-1883: critical turning moment = Creg x stem weight, Creg ~100-200 N m/kg by soil; used in GALES (Gardiner et al. 2000/2008)

uproot_sat_reduction.source: Kamimura et al. 2012, Eur. J. For. Res. 131:219-227 (tree-pulling with rapidly supplied water: anchorage ~30-50% lower on saturated soil); Peltola et al. 2000 (waterlogged soils)

snap_decay_prevalence.source: assumed/calibrated: fraction of street trees with internal decay; strength of a hollow stem = 1-(r/R)^4 (Kane & Ryan 2004, J. Arboric. 30:347-356)

snap_decay_rr_max.source: Mattheck & Breloer 1994, The Body Language of Trees: failure common when shell t/R < 0.3 (r/R > 0.7); r/R ~ U(0.3, 0.85) assumed

beaufort_twigs_ms.source: Beaufort scale force 8 (gale, 17.2-20.7 m/s): 'twigs broken from trees' (UK Met Office / WMO-No. 8)

beaufort_branches_ms.source: Beaufort scale force 9 (strong gale, 20.8-24.4 m/s): branches break, slight structural damage (UK Met Office)

leaf_area_index.source: Peper & McPherson 2003, Urban For. Urban Green. 2:19-29 (street tree LAI ~2-6)

leaf_shed_frac_max.source: assumed: storm-stripped share of leaf area at Beaufort 10+; most SF street trees are evergreen in winter

debris_cd_plate.source: Wills, Lee & Wyatt 2002, J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn. 90:555-565 (plate/sheet debris); Tachikawa 1983, JWEIA 14:443-453

debris_cd_rod.source: circular cylinder, subcritical Re (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag)

leaf_terminal_ms.source: Vogel 1994, Life in Moving Fluids, Princeton UP: falling leaves ~1-2 m/s

ground_restitution.source: assumed (inelastic debris impacts; Lin, Holmes & Letchford 2007, J. Struct. Eng. 133:274 use rest after first impact)

ground_friction.source: assumed Coulomb friction for debris on wet pavement

inlet_capture_radius_m.source: team spec (CONTRACT v3): leaf litter landing within ~5 m of a grate is swept onto it by gutter flow

inlet_grate_area_m2.source: ~0.6 x 0.9 m SF catch-basin grate (data/grid/meta.json sources.inlets; FHWA HEC-22 3rd ed.)

inlet_clog_max.source: FHWA HEC-22 3rd ed. sec. 4.4: design clogging factor 50% for sag grates; up to ~80% observed in leaf-fall storms (assumed upper bound)

car_mass_kg.source: US EPA Automotive Trends Report 2023: average new car ~1,800 kg incl. SUVs; sedan ~1,400 kg

car_clearance_m.source: typical sedan ground clearance (Shu et al. 2011)

car_seal_frac.source: Martinez-Gomariz et al. 2018, J. Flood Risk Manag. 11:S817-S826: water ingress reduces buoyancy; gives float depth ~0.35-0.5 m, in the 0.3-0.6 m range of experiments

car_cd_side.source: Shu, Xia, Falconer & Lin 2011, J. Hydraul. Res. 49:709-717 (drag on partially submerged vehicles ~1.1)

car_friction.source: Shu et al. 2011 / Xia et al. 2014, Nat. Hazards 70:1619-1630: tyre-ground friction 0.25-0.75; 0.25 conservative (wet, parked in gear)

car_drift_frac.source: assumed: an unstable car moves at ~80% of the local depth-averaged velocity

fall_noise_deg.source: assumed scatter of fall direction around the local wind (gust direction variability ~10-20 deg, ESDU 85020)

prune_area_factor.source: ANSI A300 Part 1 (2017) pruning standard: crown reduction/thinning removes <=25% of live foliage per cycle; Pavlis et al. 2008, Arboric. Urban For. 34:102 (wind-tunnel drag reduction after thinning/reduction)

brace_strength_factor.source: assumed: ANSI A300 Part 3 supplemental support (cabling/bracing) limits stem/codominant failure; 25% effective capacity gain (Smiley & Kane 2006, Arboric. Urban For. 32:33 report reduced failure of cabled stems)

tree_load_factor.source: calibrated so the inventory's sound (defect-free) trees break at a median crown gust of 42 m/s (Virot et al. 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93:023001). Bundles, each within its published range: dynamic (sway) amplification 1.3-1.6 (Gardiner et al. 2008, Forestry 81:447-463), overhanging crown weight 1.1-1.2 (Peltola et al. 1999, Can. J. For. Res. 29:647-661), open-grown crown silhouette vs inventory allometry ~1.5-2 (McPherson et al. 2016 Urban Tree Database)

uproot_calib_factor.source: calibrated: multiplies Creg so the 31.12.2022 replay reproduces the 9 SF 311 'tree down/damaged' reports inside the tile (data/grid/validation.json); placeholder until calibration run
